analysis.title: Marketcolour + FOMC/Budget/Earnings, 29 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities closed higher Wednesday: SPX +28bps to 7743 (8 of 11 sectors up, Tech +0.48%, Utilities -0.88%), NDX +55bps to 29813, RTY +41bps to 2830.

Wednesday was the first real day of rotation back into AI in recent weeks, after capital raise overhangs (META, SPCX) cleared and better tech prints came in overnight (SKHY, VRT) plus ORCL +10%. The GS Data Center Basket (GSTMTDAT) rose 2.59%.
MSFT rose about 4% after hours after fiscal Q1 revenue beat. ORCL +10% after reaffirming its positive 2027 guide at its investor day.
In Europe, UK Banks (GSSBBKDU +1.8%, after the Budget), EU Power names (GSXEPOWR +1.4%) and EU Semis (GSSBSEMI +1.3%) outperformed.

FOMC held the funds rate at 3.75-4.00% as expected. GS reads Fed commentary as a compromise to hike every other meeting, expects a second and final hike in December, and sees a third hike in March as possible if inflation is higher than GS expects.
GS expects the ECB to deliver one more 25bp hike in December, taking the policy rate to a 2.75% peak.

UK Budget broadly matched expectations. Higher debt interest costs pushed up the OBR deficit projections and cut fiscal space. The Chancellor announced tax increases raising £6bn per year by 2029/30, temporary cost-of-living measures and funding for the Defence Investment Plan.

Airbus (Buy, PT EUR240, +25% upside): Q3 adjusted EBIT of €1,768mn was about 1% below consensus on revenue of €17.47bn, about 2% below. FCF before customer financing was -€102mn vs company-compiled consensus of +€325mn. Guidance of about 870 deliveries was confirmed and the FY26 outlook is unchanged.

Airbus management said it is comfortable with 870 plus or minus 20 deliveries, with known risks included in guidance. P&W engines remain the pacing item, but nothing has put planned 2027/2028 output at risk.
SocGen beat and made a small raise. GS sees mid-single-digit upgrades to 2026 consensus earnings, probably unchanged for outer years, and the stock up 2-3%, though it may not hold.
ING missed on net profit by 6%, across nearly all lines. GS expects the stock down 3-5%.

Prysmian beat and raised, with mixed details. EBITDA beat by 7%, driven by a 20% beat in Electrification. Transmission was a small beat, Digital Solutions (fibre) missed on a light top line, and Power Grid missed on margins. Quarterly FCF was light but the FY FCF guide was raised. The EBITDA guide midpoint rose to 3.1bn, implying about 6% upgrades to consensus.

MTU Aero Q3 was in line, with EBIT a 1% miss on weaker OEM while commercial MRO was strong. FCF of 172m beat consensus of 109m, and the FCF upgrade should be well received ahead of the capital markets day.

WPP beat and reiterated guidance with a positive bias. Q3 organic net sales were -2.1% vs GSe -3.3% and Vuma consensus -3.2%. Net sales of £2,411m were about 1% ahead of expectations. WPP Media (47% of 2025 net sales) returned to +0.3% growth from -2.8% in Q2.

GOOGL (Buy, PT cut from $435 to $385): Q3 2026 revenue was $127.6bn (+25% y/y), in line with consensus. Search & Other was $63.35bn (+12%), YouTube Ads $11.21bn, and Google Cloud $30.71bn (+103%). Operating income was $40.6bn vs consensus $43.4bn.

MSFT (Conviction Buy, PT $700, 30% upside): fiscal Q1 (September) revenue was $92.3bn (+19% cc y/y), 2% above the Street. Non-GAAP EPS was $4.89 (+27% y/y), 3% above the Street. GS says AI-ecosystem investor focus has shifted to the sustainability of token demand and the depth of financing markets.
Basket idea: GS reiterates its bullish AI view and highlights the rebalanced AI Health Care Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCAIP), which has low correlation to AI, the opposite of AI, rates and oil.
